**Answer: 807**

**Reduction.** Write $n = (c\cdot m)$ with all factors of 2 and 5 removed. Since $10^t-1$ is coprime to 10, $\frac{10^t-1}{cm}$ is short exactly when $n \mid 10^t-1$, i.e. when $\operatorname{ord}_n(10)\mid t$. So the minimal $t$ for which the fraction is short is $t=\operatorname{ord}_n(10)$, and $t$ is $m$-tastic exactly when $t=\operatorname{ord}_{n_c}(10)$ for some $c\in\{1,\dots,2017\}$. (If $n=1$, the minimal $t$ is 1.)

**Upper bound.** The value $n_c$ depends only on the part of $c$ coprime to 10, call it $c'$, so $n_c = m'c'$ with $m'$ the 10-free part of $m$. Each $c'$ is itself an integer in $[1,2017]$ coprime to 10, so there are at most
$$|A| = \#\{1\le x\le 2017 : \gcd(x,10)=1\} = 201\cdot 4 + 3 = 807$$
possible values of $c'$. Hence $|S(m)|\le 807$.

**Attaining the bound.** Choose $m$ so that the map $c'\mapsto \operatorname{ord}_{m'c'}(10)$ is injective on $A$. Let $m'=\prod_{p\le 2017,\ p\ne 2,5} p^{E_p}$ with each $E_p$ very large. For $a\in A$, the exponent of $p$ in $\operatorname{ord}_{m'a}(10)$ is $E_p+v_p(a)+(\text{constant depending on }p)$, because $\operatorname{ord}_{p^k}(10)$ grows like $p^{k}$ times a fixed factor, while the contribution of the other prime powers to the $p$-exponent is bounded independently of $E_p$. So the order determines $v_p(a)$ for every $p$, hence determines $a$. Thus all 807 values of $c'$ give distinct $t$-values, and $|S(m)|=807$.

ANSWER: 807
